weaponAmmo.Title: Weapon with ammunition
weaponAmmo.Summary: A bow whose every shot spends an arrow, impossible once the quiver is empty.

Steps.Type: A “Weapon” Definition type with the pool capability.
Steps.Weapon: The “Bow” Definition holds an “ammo” pool from 0 to 20.
Steps.Condition: The “Has ammunition” Condition checks the pool is above 0.
Steps.Cost: The “Spend ammunition” Effect removes 1 from the pool.
Steps.Action: The “Shoot” Action requires the Condition and pays the Effect as its cost.

consumable.Title: Consumable
consumable.Summary: A three-dose potion: drinking costs a dose and restores 4 vitality, never above the maximum.

Steps.Type: A “Resource” Definition type with the pool capability.
Steps.Doses: The “Healing potion” holds a “doses” pool from 0 to 3.
Steps.Vitality: “Vitality” holds an “hit points” pool from 0 to 12, starting at 6.
Steps.CostAndEffect: One Effect removes a dose (the cost), another adds 4 hit points (the effect). The pool bounds the result.
Steps.Action: The “Drink” Action requires a dose left.

xpProgression.Title: Experience progression
xpProgression.Summary: Accumulated experience points and a computed level: one level every 1000 points.

Steps.Type: A “Progression” Definition type with the value capability.
Steps.Experience: The “Experience” Definition stores the points earned.
Steps.Level: The “Points per level” Parameter (1000) and the “Level” Formula = floor(experience ÷ points per level) + 1.
Steps.Action: The “Award experience” Action applies the Effect.

encumbrance.Title: Encumbrance
encumbrance.Summary: A carrying capacity computed from Strength, and an “Overloaded” Condition when the load exceeds it.

Steps.Type: An “Attribute” Definition type with the value capability.
Steps.Capacity: The “Capacity per Strength point” Parameter (10) and the “Carrying capacity” Formula = Strength × that parameter.
Steps.Overloaded: The “Overloaded” Condition is true when the load exceeds the capacity. Use it in a Permission rule or a Modifier.

ruleset.Summary: The Ruleset holds a game's whole configuration: its types, rules and contents.
ruleset.Usage: Work in a draft, publish once “Publish readiness” reports nothing, then activate the version to play it.

definitionType.Summary: A Definition type describes a family of game elements (attribute, skill, resource…): its capabilities and fields.
definitionType.Usage: For each capability, choose whether it is unavailable, optional, on by default or required. This type's description serves as help in the editor of its Definitions.

definition.Summary: A Definition is a concrete game element of a type: Strength, Bow, Vitality…
definition.Usage: Its capabilities (value, pool, collection, state) decide what Formulas can read and what Effects can change.

parameter.Summary: A Parameter is a typed Ruleset constant, reusable everywhere.
parameter.Usage: Prefer a Parameter to a hard-coded number: it changes in one place.

formula.Summary: A Formula computes a value from Parameters, other Formulas, references and the context.
formula.Usage: Its result type is checked: a “number” Formula cannot produce text.

formulaBinding.Summary: A derived output computes a Definition output with a Formula instead of storing it.
formulaBinding.Usage: The output then becomes read-only: no Effect can write it.

condition.Summary: A Condition is an expression that produces true or false.
condition.Usage: Actions, Outcomes, Triggers, Permission rules and Modifiers use it to decide.

roll.Summary: A Roll is a dice roll described by a safe formula (for example 1d20 or 2d6+1).
roll.Usage: A Test uses it; a Test can also skip the Roll and start from a Formula.

outcome.Summary: An Outcome is a possible result of a Test (success, failure, critical…).
outcome.Usage: The first Outcome whose Condition is true wins, by decreasing priority.

test.Summary: A Test reads typed inputs, optionally rolls, computes a total and a margin, then picks an Outcome.
test.Usage: The Test's Formulas read its values in variables.test (inputs, total, target, margin).

effect.Summary: An Effect changes a mutable Definition output with an operation (set, add, subtract, multiply, toggle).
effect.Usage: The target must be mutable and the operand of a compatible type.

action.Summary: An Action is what a player or the GM triggers: Conditions, costs, an optional Test, then Effects.
action.Usage: If a Condition is false nothing is written. Costs are paid before effects. An acquisition Action adds Definitions to the character before its effects. With several targets, costs are paid once and the Test, Effects and Table run for each target.

permissionPolicy.Summary: A Permission decides who may read, write, execute or configure what. The GM always has every right.
permissionPolicy.Usage: The most specific scope decides (one object, then a kind of object, then the Ruleset). Among its matching rules (role, minimum ownership, users, Condition), the highest priority wins and DENY wins a tie; otherwise the default effect applies. Without any Permission, Foundry ownership decides.

eventType.Summary: An Event type describes a game fact (attack resolved, turn started…) and its data.
eventType.Usage: Triggers react to Events; Actions can emit them.

trigger.Summary: A Trigger reacts to an Event type: it filters, checks its Conditions, then runs Actions.
trigger.Usage: Everything goes through Actions. Who acts: the one who caused the event, or the one it aimed at for a reaction (parry, thorns). Offered: the Actions are proposed to who acts instead of running. A reroll Action run this way replays the use that caused the event; keep the dice for a Shield spell.

contentType.Summary: A content type describes elements stored in Foundry (items, spells, gear…) and their fields.
contentType.Usage: Choose whether they live as Items or Actors, and under which subtype.

contentTemplate.Summary: A content template is a concrete element ready to be given to a character.
contentTemplate.Usage: It can grant Definitions and Actions, and offer choices on acquisition. Its optional acquisition Action adds its Conditions and costs to the acquisition, in a single write.

modifier.Summary: A Modifier adjusts a final value (bonus, penalty, cap) while its Conditions are true.
modifier.Usage: A Modifier that no Action applies works everywhere, while its Conditions are true. A Modifier applied by an Action only works on the Actor that received it, for its duration. Stacking rules decide whether several Modifiers add up or the best one wins.

duration.Summary: A Duration says how long a state lasts: instant, fixed, until an Event, while a Condition holds, until removed or until a date.
duration.Usage: Pick a mode: only the fields that mode needs are shown. A world time is counted in seconds.

creationSystem.Summary: A creation system describes the steps of creating a character.
creationSystem.Usage: Each step offers a choice of definitions or contents, points to spread, a roll, or a final review. A step can depend on a Condition, and the last steps can repeat term after term (careers, lifepaths).

progressionSystem.Summary: A progression system says how a character grows: advancements bought with XP or points, and milestones reached at a level.
progressionSystem.Usage: An advancement raises a Definition and pays a cost Formula from a currency; its cost can grow with the current value. A milestone grants Definitions and runs an Action once its Condition holds; an Action input lets the player choose (a feat). Levels themselves are a Formula over the XP.

sheetDefinition.Summary: A sheet is what players see on an Actor or an Item: tabs, sections, lists of the Definitions they hold, values and Action buttons.
sheetDefinition.Usage: Click a block of the sheet to change it in the tools on the left. Under “Add”, click a block or an element of the Ruleset to add it into the selection, or drag it onto the sheet; drag the sheet's blocks to move them. Without any sheet, Actors and Items show the automatic layout. Players choose “Rule Them'All sheet” in Foundry's sheet choice.

category.Summary: A category classifies Definitions and contents for filtering.
category.Usage: The catalog is managed here; elements store only the id.

tag.Summary: A tag freely marks any Ruleset object.

table.Summary: A Table turns a roll into a result: critical hits, wild magic, random encounters, injuries.
table.Usage: Pick the Roll and an optional bonus, then give each row its range and the Actions it runs. An Action rolls the Table after its Effects; the row's Actions run in the same step.

die.Summary: A Die has faces of its own: narrative dice with symbols, a d6 whose 1 is a special face, a stunt die.
die.Usage: Give it a letter, then its counters and its faces. A Roll throws it with that letter (2dp for two dice). A Formula reads a counter over all the dice thrown; a negative count cancels (a failure counts -1 success).

scale.Summary: A Description scale turns a number into words: "Seems in great shape", "Badly hurt", "Exceptional".
scale.Usage: Give each band its range and words. Link the scale to a Definition type (all its Definitions) or to one Definition. On a sheet, a value shown "As a description" shows these words instead of the number, for observers for instance.

StackingMode.replace: Last in order within its group

Permission.NoRules: No rules: the default effect applies.
Permission.Precedence: The policy with the most specific scope decides. Among its matching rules the highest priority wins, and Deny wins a tie. If no rule matches, the default effect applies.

Roll.VariantsHelp: While its Condition is true, a variant replaces the dice formula (two dice keeping the best, for example). The first true variant wins. A formula can read @content.<field>, @input.<id> and @test.<id>.

ActionInput.Title: Choices when used
ActionInput.Help: Values the player or the GM chooses each time the Action is used (a slot level, a difficulty). Formulas, Conditions and dice read them as variables.input.<id> or @input.<id>.
ActionInput.Label: Label
ActionInput.OptionsPlaceholder: One per line: value = label (empty: any value)

Table.RowsHelp: Each row covers a range of totals. Leave a bound empty for an open end. Ranges must not overlap.

TurnOrder.now: Acts now, before the current turn

Progression.AdvancementsHelp: What a character buys with a currency (XP, points): each purchase raises one Definition by the step. The cost Formula reads variables.advance.current and variables.advance.next.
Progression.Label: Label
Progression.MilestonesHelp: Reached when their Condition holds (a level): they grant their Definitions and run their Action once per character. The Action's inputs are the choices of that milestone.

Initiative.Help: Actors under this Ruleset roll this Test, or draw a row of this Table, in the combat tracker; the result is their initiative.

Shared.Help: Definitions held once for the whole table, outside the characters: a GM reserve, clocks, a die every combat shares. Effects and Formulas reach them with the World and Combat roles.

Group.Help: A group Test is made by each member before the Action's own Test; Formulas read the results in variables.group (count, best, worst, sum, outcomes). A linked role is the first Actor of a collection of references, such as the vehicle a pilot crews.
Group.MembersChosen: Chosen when the Action is used

Test.ExtraRollsHelp: After the Roll, each extra roll whose Condition holds adds to the roll total or takes from it (a 10 adds a die, a 1 takes one away).

Die.LetterHelp: One lowercase letter, other than c, d or f, which Foundry keeps for its own dice.
Die.CountersHelp: What the faces count, like Success or Advantage. Dice sharing a counter name add up.
Die.FacesHelp: One card per face, in order. A count can be negative to cancel another die's symbol.
